categories.name: It works
categories.notes:
Build succeeds; the 10 warnings are the scaffold's ImageSharp NuGet advisories, none introduced (5/5). / returns 200 through the '/' domain on the published Blog page (blogFrontPage), with a hero, an intro and a 'Latest posts' grid. Both post cards show date, title, excerpt and a working link (10/10). Both posts render every block (hero, rich text, image + caption, rich text) with no 'Could not render' text, but the rich text block, used on every page, prints its HTML escaped: literal

, and tags show as text. Views/Shared/Components/RichText/Default.cshtml writes @Model.Html, an IHtmlEncodedString, without Html.Raw, and Razor encodes it. The stored markup is correct (6/10). All 5 media items are the provided Unsplash photos, imported into an 'Unsplash' media folder and served through signed GetCropUrl URLs that load (5/5). The domain '/' is on the Blog page and all content is published (5/5).

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: heroBlock, richTextBlock and imageBlock are element types in Blocks/; blogFrontPage and blogPost are document types in Pages/ (8/8). One 'Blog Block Grid' data type (12 columns) in Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid with hero (heading, subheading, background image), rich text and image (image, caption) is used on both page types. Posts are split into 4 blocks with an 8/4 text and image row (7/7). siteRoot is the only root type, siteRoot -> blogFrontPage -> blogPost, both templates are assigned, and aliases are English camelCase (5/5). There are no compositions. Post date and excerpt are real properties, and there are no duplicated or orphaned types (5/5). There is no listing-image property, but the cards still show date and excerpt, which is acceptable.

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: blogFrontPage.cshtml and blogPost.cshtml render with Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "blocks"); there are no custom loops, and the scaffold's blockgrid partials are untouched (7/7). Three markup-free adapters at Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/{heroBlock,richTextBlock,imageBlock}.cshtml take BlockGridItem<T>, map to plain models and call Component.InvokeAsync (6/6). There is one ViewComponent per block (Hero, RichText, Image) in Components/, each rendering Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml, with models in Models/Blocks/. However, RichTextModel exposes Umbraco's IHtmlEncodedString (Umbraco.Cms.Core.Strings), so the RichText component view still depends on an Umbraco type; this is also what leads to the escaping bug (6/7). Program.cs and appsettings.json are unchanged, there are no migrations, no .cs in the Models root, friendly Children<T>()/Url()/GetCropUrl and no injected services; styling goes through Tailwind into wwwroot/dist/site.css (5/5).

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Two on-topic posts: 'Why MCP Is Awesome: One Protocol, Every Tool' (M x N to M + N, JSON-RPC, vendor neutrality) and 'MCP in Practice: The Site You Are Reading Right Now' (this site was built over MCP). Both are accurate, use relevant credited photos (code, circuit board, puzzle piece, cubes) and are spread over 4 blocks, but they are short (~220 and ~195 words in 4 paragraphs each), and the second is mostly self-referential (3/6). Presentation: the header, footer and front-page cards look clean, but the model's own block-grid CSS in Umbraco.Bench.Frontend/src/site.css makes both .umb-block-grid and its inner .umb-block-grid__layout-container 12-column grids. The layout container lands in one column of the outer grid, which collapses to the 11 gaps (264px). So every hero, text and image block is squeezed into a ~260px strip on the left of the page: post bodies read as a long narrow column, and the 4/12 image is a thumbnail with its caption wrapping a word per line. Post pages also repeat the title as a hero h1 under the page h1. It does not read like a real blog (1/4).

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: All schema, media and content went through the Umbraco MCP server (40 calls, 22 writes; no Management API, DB, uSync, browser or migrations). Order was model -> content -> Razor with stop/build/restart, with no warnings. It stayed in the project folder (its own task output in AppData Temp and /tmp curl scratch only), with no memory access and no reads of results/ or tests/ (3/3). The final report opens with 'Everything is built, published, and verified end to end' and states that verification found no problems. Its verification was a curl/grep check that never looked at the page, so it missed the escaped HTML on every page and the collapsed grid layout, and discloses neither. The other details (types, blocks, URLs, the build fix) are accurate (0/2).

summary: A correctly modeled MCP-built blog: 3 blocks, front page and post types filed right, '/' domain, Unsplash media, and a textbook adapter -> ViewComponent pipeline. But the rich text component prints its HTML escaped on every page, and the model's custom block-grid CSS squeezes every block into a ~260px column, so the site looks broken, and the final report claimed it was verified end to end.
strengths: Clean schema: 3 element types in Blocks/, 2 page types in Pages/, one block grid data type in Custom/, correct siteRoot -> blogFrontPage -> blogPost hierarchy
Conventional rendering pipeline: GetBlockGridHtmlAsync, markup-free adapters, one ViewComponent per block, untouched scaffold partials
Provided Unsplash photos imported into a media folder and served through signed GetCropUrl URLs, credited in captions
Fast and focused: 8 minutes, 40 MCP calls, the order of operations followed, stayed in the project folder
